title: US solar’s foundation holds strong, even as the ground keeps shifting
gist: US solar installed 11.4 GWdc in Q2 2026 (+45% YoY), driven almost entirely by utility-scale developers racing to energise a 200+ GWdc safe-harbored pipeline before the Section 48E/45Y deadlines, while residential collapsed to a five-year-low 995 MWdc after the 25D credit expired. Wood Mackenzie holds a flat ~44 GWdc/year base case through 2031 because permitting (30% of the early-stage pipeline), interconnection and a new 15% tariff-plus-minimum-import-price regime cap how fast demand converts into steel in the ground.

insights.claim: The US solar industry installed 11.4 GWdc in Q2 2026, up 45% year-over-year and 43% sequentially from a seasonally weak Q1.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: The headline growth rate is a deadline artefact, not underlying demand acceleration — do not extrapolate the +45% into 2027 run-rates.
insights.quote: The US solar industry installed 11.4 gigawatts direct current (GWdc) of capacity in Q2 2026, a 45% increase from Q2 2025 and a 43% increase from Q1 2026.
insights.locator: The US solar industry installed 11.4 gigawatts

insights.claim: Utility-scale solar installed nearly 10 GWdc in Q2 2026, a 61% year-over-year increase, as developers rushed to energise safe-harbored projects ahead of Section 48E/45Y tax credit deadlines.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: Utility-scale EPC and module order books are front-loaded; expect a volume air-pocket once the safe-harbor cohort is placed in service.
insights.locator: The race to place safe-harbored projects in service

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie estimates the safe-harbored US solar project pipeline exceeds 200 GWdc, which is what underpins the near-term installation outlook regardless of policy noise.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: A 200+ GWdc backlog against ~44 GWdc/year of installs is roughly 4-5 years of visible volume — a durable floor for module, tracker and inverter demand.
insights.quote: The size of the safe-harbored project pipeline, which Wood Mackenzie estimates totals over 200 GWdc, continues to underpin the near-term outlook.
insights.locator: The size of the safe-harbored project pipeline

insights.claim: The July 4, 2026 begin-construction deadline has passed, so developers who missed it must place projects in service by December 31, 2027 or lose tax credit eligibility entirely.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: A hard 31 Dec 2027 cliff creates a scramble for EPC labour, interconnection slots and equipment through 2027 — and a visible cost-inflation window for suppliers.
insights.locator: The July 4, 2026 begin-construction deadline has now passed

insights.claim: Utility-scale contracting activity is concentrating in a handful of markets, notably Utah and Texas, rather than spreading evenly across the country.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: Geographic concentration means ERCOT and Utah interconnection and land costs become the binding constraints on national volume.
insights.locator: Contracting activity remained resilient in the utility-scale segment

insights.claim: Data and technology companies account for the majority of new utility-scale solar offtake agreements, making data centre demand the dominant driver of new US solar development.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: US utility-scale solar is now a derivative of hyperscaler capex — a pause in AI datacentre buildout would transmit directly into solar offtake volumes.
insights.quote: Data and technology companies continue to account for the majority of new offtake agreements
insights.locator: Contracting activity remained resilient in the utility-scale segment

insights.claim: New US residential solar installations totalled just 995 MWdc in Q2 2026, the segment's lowest quarterly total in five years.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: Sub-1 GW quarters imply severe revenue compression for residential installers and loan originators — watch for consolidation and credit stress.
insights.locator: New residential solar installations totaled just 995 MWdc

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie now expects a 23% year-over-year contraction in US residential solar in 2026, a steeper decline than its prior quarter's estimate, before growth resumes in 2027.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: The downgrade direction matters more than the level — consensus residential forecasts are still being marked down, so avoid catching the falling knife before 2027 visibility.
insights.locator: We now expect a 23% year-over-year contraction in 2026

insights.claim: After the Section 25D expiration, residential installers face operational, not demand, bottlenecks as they shift business models from cash and loan sales to third-party ownership.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: TPO-capable platforms with tax equity access take share from loan-dependent installers — a structural winner/loser split inside the same segment.
insights.quote: installers are working through the operational challenges of shifting from cash and loans sales to third-party ownership
insights.locator: Following the Section 25D tax credit expiration

insights.claim: US commercial solar installations rose 11% year-over-year in Q2 2026, driven by continued NEM 2.0 buildout in California.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: Commercial growth is legacy-tariff-dependent; California NEM 2.0 queue exhaustion is a dated risk to watch.
insights.locator: Commercial solar installations increased 11% year-over-year

insights.claim: Community solar installations declined 14% year-over-year in Q2 2026 as a steep drop in New York volumes offset growth in Illinois, New Jersey, Virginia and Delaware.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: Community solar is a state-policy trade, not a national one — single-state program design changes swing the whole segment.
insights.locator: Community solar installations declined 14% year-over-year

insights.claim: Non-residential distributed solar retains tax credit eligibility and strong pipelines, but state-level policy changes and interconnection timelines — not demand — are what cap its growth.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: In distributed solar the bottleneck has migrated from economics to queue throughput; interconnection-reform catalysts are the upside trigger.
insights.locator: The non-residential distributed solar segments benefit

insights.claim: A proclamation signed on August 6, 2026 imposes a 15% tariff plus minimum import prices on key solar components, effective December 4, 2026.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: A price floor plus tariff is far more binding than a tariff alone — it removes the ability of foreign suppliers to absorb duties, so module ASPs reset upward from December 2026.
insights.locator: On August 6, 2026, the administration signed a proclamation

insights.claim: The new tariff-plus-minimum-import-price structure widens the advantage for fully integrated domestic solar suppliers while raising the financing bar for standalone cell and wafer capacity.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: Long vertically integrated US manufacturers versus single-step cell/wafer entrants; the latter need higher, longer-dated price assumptions to finance.
insights.quote: This new structure widens the advantage for fully integrated domestic suppliers and raises the financing bar for cell and wafer capacity.
insights.locator: On August 6, 2026, the administration signed a proclamation

insights.claim: On July 28, 2026 the FCC added foreign-produced power inverters to its Covered List, barring new authorisations for unapproved models.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: Inverter supply is now a national-security-gated market; approved domestic inverter vendors gain a regulatory moat overnight.
insights.locator: Separately, on July 28, 2026, the FCC added

insights.claim: An August 26, 2026 Executive Order restricts imports of power generation equipment from Covered Foreign Entities including China, with final impact still pending outstanding guidance.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: Unresolved guidance is itself the tradeable event — clarification dates are catalysts for both developer cost curves and domestic equipment names.
insights.locator: Additionally, on August 26, 2026, the White House issued an Executive Order

insights.claim: Further restrictions on foreign products may catalyse a new wave of domestic utility-scale solar and storage manufacturing investment in the US.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: Trade escalation is a capex catalyst for US factory announcements — but the author flags it as conditional, so treat announced capacity as optionality not certainty.
insights.locator: further restrictions on foreign products may catalyse

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's base case has US annual solar additions stabilising at roughly 44 GWdc on average through 2031, essentially flat rather than growing.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: A flat-volume market means solar equipment earnings must come from price and mix, not unit growth — favours pricing-power assets over volume-levered ones.
insights.quote: Annual installations will remain essentially flat, hovering around 44 GWdc on average.
insights.locator: In our base case, solar additions stabilise

insights.claim: US cumulative solar capacity will roughly double over the next five years to over 545 GWdc by 2031.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: Doubling the installed base doubles the O&M, repowering and inverter-replacement service pool — an underfollowed recurring-revenue pocket.
insights.locator: The US solar market will roughly double

insights.claim: Permitting delays now affect an estimated 30% of the early-stage US utility-scale solar pipeline, making permitting a first-order constraint alongside interconnection and trade policy.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: Nearly a third of early-stage projects at permitting risk justifies discounting headline pipeline figures heavily when underwriting developer NAVs.
insights.quote: Permitting delays now affect an estimated 30% of the early-stage utility-scale pipeline
insights.locator: Despite growth, uncertainty remains elevated

insights.claim: Despite a sharp Q2 installation beat, the 2031 outlook changed only minimally quarter-over-quarter, implying near-term upside is pull-forward from later years rather than incremental demand.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: Treat strong quarterly installation prints as timing, not upgrades — the cumulative forecast is the number that matters for long-cycle capacity decisions.
insights.locator: Despite a sharp increase in Q2 installations

insights.claim: The post-2030 US solar outlook is materially more uncertain because developers have flagged how challenging project economics become without the ITC.
insights.speaker: Caitlin Connelly
insights.so_what: Terminal-value assumptions in US solar developer models past 2030 are the soft spot — stress-test them for a no-ITC world.
insights.locator: The post-2030 outlook is even more uncertain
